facts.fact: North-facing beach surrounded by rocky headland; one of four pocket beaches on the Cape Moreton peninsula.
Lies between Cape Moreton and North Point, edged by about 15 m bluffs; known as hazardous with rips, hidden rocks and big waves (from search summary of Queensland Parks wording, not fetched).
Listed as a picnic stop on the Northern Island discovery drive; reached by 4WD, which needs a Moreton Island Recreation Area vehicle access permit.

name: North Point
correct_wikipedia_title: none (en.wikipedia 'North Point' is Hong Kong; no Queensland article found; 'Cape Moreton' / Moreton Island National Park cover it)

facts.fact: Protected cove on the north-west side of Cape Moreton, home of the Champagne Pools, a natural ocean pool hollowed out among the rocks, and North Point Light.
Open fires are not permitted at North Point campground, which is within walking distance of the lighthouse and Honeymoon Bay (search summary of Queensland Parks).
Reached by personal 4WD or 4WD bus tour from Tangalooma.
On the incoming tide water cascades over the rocks at the Champagne Pools (Queensland Parks wording via search summary).

name: Kings Beach
coordinates_source: placement pin from input.json (resolved earlier); not re-resolved

facts.fact: Very popular patrolled beach with the Caloundra (Mets) Surf Club at the northern end of the precinct.
Kings Beach Ocean Pool at the northern end is a 25 m seawater pool with disabled access and a children's wading area.
Large green spaces, playgrounds, cafes and restaurants beside the beach; main patrolled surf beach with a webcam.
Bulcock Beach is reached from Kings Beach by a boardwalk over the rocks; Caloundra Lighthouses sit at Kings Beach.
